# A `Transaction` block with no `PaymentSplit` under it.
#
# The directive's children are its splits — that is what it is for, and what
# distinguishes it from `txn_guid:`, which says the same thing in one key.
# Written childless it says nothing the key does not, and it is read by nobody:
# with no children the block scores a bare slot, so the comparison pairs it on
# date, amount and memo, and an otherwise-matching record reports `unchanged`
# before the override that would have preferred the directive, or the note
# saying the keys went unread, ever runs.
#
# That is the same silent unread line a mistyped directive guid and a
# `from_credit:` block naming a `Transaction` are both refused for.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the transaction, with nothing
# attached.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    memo: "Wire"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
